pages.title: Observatory night mode
pages.summary: The lantern console requires the beacon feature flag for night mode.
pages.body:
Night mode in the Observatory is enabled with the beacon feature flag. The lantern console still draws its classic palette without that flag.

**Why:** The new palette renderer has not shipped to every console.

**How to apply:** Enable beacon before testing the dark theme.

**Falsified by:** Every supported console rendering night mode without beacon.

pages.title: Cache generation fencing
pages.summary: The comet cache rejects stale writers using CACHE_EPOCH_MISMATCH.
pages.body:
The comet cache increments its generation whenever the index is rebuilt. A writer with an older generation fails with CACHE_EPOCH_MISMATCH rather than overwriting the new index.

**Why:** A slow writer can finish after another process replaces the cache.

**How to apply:** Reopen the cache and retry after CACHE_EPOCH_MISMATCH.

**Falsified by:** Stale writers safely committing without a generation check.

pages.title: Atomic atlas exports
pages.summary: Atlas exports use a temporary file and atomic rename.
pages.body:
An atlas export writes a temporary file, flushes it, then atomically renames it over the destination. Readers see the complete old export or the complete new export.

**Why:** Direct writes allowed readers to observe a partially written map.

**How to apply:** Use publish_atlas_atomically for every map export.

**Falsified by:** A reader observing a partial map through the atomic export path.

pages.title: Atlas export locking
pages.summary: Atlas exporters hold the atlas.lock lease until publication completes.
pages.body:
Atlas exporters acquire atlas.lock before creating a temporary map and hold the lease until the final rename completes. A second exporter waits for the first publication to finish.

**Why:** Atomic rename alone does not serialize two concurrent map exporters.

**How to apply:** Hold the export lease around publish_atlas_atomically.

**Falsified by:** Concurrent exports preserving publication order without the lease.

pages.title: Copper courier transport
pages.summary: The retired copper courier used polling for parcel delivery.
pages.body:
The copper courier used COPPER_POLL_INTERVAL to poll for parcels every thirty seconds. This polling transport is retired.

**Why:** Polling once every thirty seconds made parcel delivery too slow.

**How to apply:** Read the replacement transport decision.

pages.title: Courier stream transport
pages.summary: Courier deliveries now use persistent streams with resume cursors.
pages.body:
Courier deliveries use persistent streams with a resume cursor. Reconnecting starts after the last acknowledged parcel; the receiver deduplicates parcel identifiers.

**Why:** Persistent streams reduce delivery delay and resume reliably after a disconnect.

**How to apply:** Persist the acknowledged cursor before requesting the next parcel.

**Falsified by:** Lost parcels or duplicate delivery after reconnecting with the saved cursor.

pages.title: Fern parser nesting limit
pages.summary: The Fern parser rejects nesting deeper than 64 levels.
pages.body:
The Fern configuration parser limits nesting to 64 levels and reports FERN_DEPTH_LIMIT when input exceeds that limit.

**Why:** An unbounded recursive parser can exhaust the stack.

**How to apply:** Keep nested Fern maps within 64 levels; do not retry the same invalid input.

**Falsified by:** The supported parser safely accepting deeper nesting.

pages.title: Fictional test clock
pages.summary: Clock-dependent tests inject a frozen time source.
pages.body:
Tests in the Solstice project inject a frozen clock rather than reading wall time. Test fixtures advance the clock explicitly to exercise expiry boundaries.

**Why:** Tests that sleep until expiry become slow and fail intermittently.

**How to apply:** Pass FixedClock into the expiry evaluator and advance it in the test.

**Falsified by:** Expiry tests being stable while depending directly on wall time.

pages.title: Offline model cache
pages.summary: The Acorn search engine verifies its cached model checksum before loading.
pages.body:
Acorn search verifies the cached model checksum before loading weights. An absent model produces MODEL_CACHE_MISSING; a mismatched checksum produces MODEL_DIGEST_MISMATCH. Network downloads require an explicit allow-network option.

**Why:** Offline search must not silently download or use modified model bytes.

**How to apply:** Populate the cache explicitly, then run searches without network access.

**Falsified by:** An offline search loading an unverified model or initiating a download.

pages.title: Pebble database migration
pages.summary: Pebble schema upgrades run in one transaction.
pages.body:
Pebble database migrations update table definitions and the schema version in a single transaction. If any migration statement fails, the database retains the previous schema version and tables.

**Why:** A partially applied migration can make an otherwise valid store unreadable.

**How to apply:** Wrap each complete migration in a transaction and test rollback on injected failure.

**Falsified by:** A failed migration leaving a newer version number or partially upgraded tables.
